audit.recode_to: fixed-dominant FINAL (01 001 0001 00001...), non-strict, citing Avram 2008:79-80 (Misión La Paz, on-target lect: ultimate stress at 2, 3, 4 syllables) as deciding source, with Viñas Urquiza 1974:32 (displacement to final syllable under suffixation) and Nercesian 2011:81 / 2014:80 (Bermejo: primary stress on head of rightmost iambic foot; 'suelen tener el acento en la última sílaba') as corroboration, and a caution line for Tovar 1981:172 / Hunt 1940:9 (position varies with phrase rhythm) and Claesson 1994:6 (Noctén: free stress). Alternatively 'undetermined' if the catalog register requires an on-target source stronger than an MA thesis; in no case initial.
audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: The live kind/rule (fixed initial) is StressTyp2's coding, and every primary text opened contradicts it: the Spanish that StressTyp2 itself quotes from Viñas Urquiza 1974:32 puts primary stress on the final syllable under suffixation (StressTyp2's 'first syllable' is an added gloss); Avram 2008:79-80, the only phonological description of the Güisnay/Pilcomayo lect (held, verified verbatim), states ultimate stress; Nercesian 2011 (held) and the Nercesian 2014 Manual fetched sources now (p.80, p.162) give final stress for the Bermejo variety; Tovar 1981:172 (held) says phrase rhythm. The record's own editor note already concludes fixed-initial survives under no reading, yet the kind/rule fields still carry 10 100 1000. Quotations in dq/sources are all confirmed in held files, so the problem is the coding, not the evidence: recode to fixed-final (dominant) on Avram 2008 with Viñas Urquiza/Nercesian corroboration
audit.second_reader_evidence: All of the other first reader's quote findings re-verified in held files. sources.citation: Avram, Megan Leigh Zdrojkowski. 2008. A Phonological Description of Wichí: The Dialect of Misión La Paz, Salta, Argentina. MA thesis, Eastern Michigan University, Section 4.5 (Stress), pp. 78-80. Read in full-text: PDF fetched sources from etnolinguistica.wdfiles.com (mirror of commons.emich.edu/theses/152…
sources.quote: Spanish portions translated inline above: "El acento primario marca generalmente el morfema radical cuando la base no tiene sufijos" = "primary stress generally marks the root morpheme when the base has no suffixes"; "Cuando se añaden sufijos, el acento primario se desplaza a la sílaba final" = "when suffixes are added, primary stress moves to the final syllable"; "El acento puede variar por razones de ritmo" = "stress can vary for reasons of rhythm".

sources.citation: Nercesian, Verónica. 2014. Manual teórico-práctico de gramática wichí, vol. 1. Formosa: Editorial Universidad Nacional de Formosa. 277 pp. (hdl 11336/124933)
sources.quote: 'Las palabras en wichí suelen tener el acento en la última sílaba' (p.80); verbs formed by noun incorporation instead carry main stress on the first syllable of the incorporated noun; p.162: 'Cuando le agregamos el sufijo, el acento se mueve hasta la última sílaba de la nueva palabra'. Examples are Bermejo variety; author states Pilcomayo speakers will find morpholexical but not structural differences.
sources.locator: printed p. 80 (PDF p. 93); printed p. 162 (PDF p. 175); dialect scope note PDF p. ~14 (txt lines 386-404)

sources.citation: Nercesian, Verónica. 2021. Lengua y territorio: variación histórica y dialectal del wichí/weenhayek (familia mataguaya). Revista del Museo de Antropología 13(3). doi 10.31048/1852.4826.v13.n3.28281 (hdl 11336/172749)
sources.quote: None. Dialect survey (Pilcomayeño vs Bermejeño complexes; Misión La Paz placed in the Pilcomayeño group, Weenhayek/Noctén also Pilcomayeño); isoglosses are segmental, pronominal and lexical, stress is not among them.
sources.locator: whole article (18 pp); no occurrence of 'acento'

sources.quote: Only passing remarks that stress plays no role in the segmental processes discussed; no stress rule stated. Bermejo variety.
